thread.title: Parking restrictions considered on four streets, East Ferry
thread.title_full: Parking restrictions considered on four streets, East Ferry

author: ohtadmin
title: Parking restrictions considered on four streets, East Ferry
text:
There will be a public hearing to consider restricting parking on Fox Run, Douglas Street and Knowles Court.
The town council will conduct the hearing at 6 p.m. Monday, May 4, at Town Hall. Changes to timed parking at East Ferry Wharf also will be considered. The proposed amendments to the ordinance were ordered advertised by the councilors at their April 20 meeting. The ad ran on Page 6 of the April 23 edition of The Jamestown Press.
The proposal originally presented would have banned parking on both sides of Knowles Court except for two spots on the north side immediately east of Holmes Court.
Cathy Kaiser, of 35 Knowles Court, however, said restricting parking on both sides would be detrimental to residents of her 13-unit condominium. The proposal would have eliminated parking used by house cleaners in private cars, who would have to park on a side street and “lug their gear” to the building.
Kaiser also mentioned challenges with delivery drivers and service trucks if parking on both sides were to be prohibited.
Town Administrator Ed Mello, however, quelled that concern.
“Police officers don’t ticket delivery trucks,” he said. “They don’t ticket service trucks that are actively engaged in something. We don’t view that as parking. We view that as a delivery or stopping or standing, not parking.”
The councilors — President Nancy Beye and Councilwomen Mary Glackin and Mary Meagher — ultimately approved the proposed amendment without restricted parking on the north side of Knowles Court. Vice President Erik Brine and Councilman Eddie Ross were absent from the meeting.
The amended ordinance also proposes “no parking on the west side from Valley Street to Swinburne Street” on Douglas Street. Fox Run, which is the first side street heading east from Mackerel Cove that isn’t restricted, also would have parking prohibited for its entire length on the east side.
When both sides are utilized by beachgoers, access to the 24-foot-wide cul-de-sac “becomes impossible or extremely problematic for the larger delivery vehicles or, more importantly, emergency vehicles,” George Waterman, of 23 Fox Run, wrote to the council.
Most of the parking in the lot at East Ferry, if the proposal is approved, would be limited to two hours between 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily. Parking along the southernmost section in front of the businesses also would be restricted daily to 30 minutes with the two westernmost spots limited to 15 minutes each.
The proposal also would reserve a parking space at the easternmost end “as an active 30-minute loading zone” and another parking spot reserved for the harbormaster and emergency vehicles.
